rationale: B wins because it identifies the sharpest story in the packet: "Hims & Hers won't say where its compounded semaglutide comes from." That is a real reporter question, not a company-preferred launch frame. A is strong, but "Telehealth GLP-1 plus at-home blood tests: the build of a personalized weight-loss stack" is one inch from product-description territory unless the personalization mechanism is real. B also picks the right next move: crisis posture before outreach, not just fact-checking.
gaps_in_A: The regulatory angle is useful but softened: "here's how a telehealth seller is launching anyway" frames the company response before proving it has one.

"Telehealth GLP-1 plus at-home blood tests: the build of a personalized weight-loss stack" risks dressing a feature bundle as category creation; A admits it collapses without proof but still leads with the stack.
A misses the undisclosed supplier as a standalone story angle, even though it calls it "the single biggest hole."
"A newly profitable Hims & Hers bets its margins" overstates what the facts support; there is no margin data, only public-company profitability and a new product line.
gaps_in_B: "prescription by video" is not grounded; the update says telehealth visit, not video or synchronous care.
"ongoing FDA-versus-compounders dispute that is already being reported" is a little decorated beyond the fact block; the facts say FDA flagged risks and manufacturers pushed back.
The first angle blends regulator, manufacturers, public-company status, profitability, and launch into one overloaded conflict frame.
"at the center of a consumer offering" adds emphasis the update does not prove; Hims is launching access, but centrality is not established.
